title: feat: add tiered health router code agent
author: tomdacatto
pr_body_excerpt:
## Summary

A code agent that classifies each request's difficulty with a cheap LLM call (`FAST`/`BALANCED`/`DEEP`), then resolves that tier against the **live** model catalog and its last-30-minute health — not three hardcoded model IDs.

- Modality-aware: image/audio/video parts narrow the candidate pool to models whose `input_modalities` actually declare support
- Health-aware: prefers models at or below 10% 5xx over at least 10 requests, then unproven models, then the least unhealthy; ranks by error rate and p95 latency
- No retry loop — gen already retries a model's own declared fallbacks; this router's job is picking well up front

Repository: https://github.com/tomdacatto/tiered-health-router
Callable model: **`community/tomdacatto/tiered-health-router`**

## Why this axis

Other submissions on this issue route by live free-model health, code-only complexity scoring, or a capability-fit price ladder with retry escalation. This one routes by *task difficulty*, judged by a model reading the request rather than a length/keyword heuristic, then still resolves that tier against live pricing/health instead of hardcoded IDs.

## Live demo evidence

Three real requests against the deployed agent, each landing on a different model — full commands and responses in [`demos/README.md`](https://github.com/tomdacatto/pollinations/blob/quest/15017-router-agent/apps/agent-tiered-health-router/demos/README.md):

| Request | Model used |
|---|---|
| "What is the capital of Iceland?" | `qwen/qwen3.7-flash` (cheapest eligible) |
| Compare 3 caching strategies, recommend one | `Mistral-Large-3` |
| Design a cross-region rate limiter under clock skew | `gpt-5.4` |

## Alpha feedback

- Custom response headers (`X-Router-*`) don't survive on `/v1/responses` either — a prior PR on this issue found they're dropped by the Chat Completions conversion specifically; testing against `/v1/responses` directly still showed them missing. No dashboard viewer for a code agent's `console.log` ou

gist.headline: The router reads the room
gist.blurb: A community code agent now asks a cheap model how gnarly your request is before choosing where to send it. Easy questions get a quick path; clock-skew rate limiters get the grown-up chair.
gist.summary: Added the callable community model `community/tomdacatto/tiered-health-router`, which classifies requests as FAST, BALANCED, or DEEP with a cheap LLM call and selects a live catalog model using modality support plus the last 30 minutes of health, error-rate, and p95-latency data.
gist.impact: Developers can route simple prompts to economical eligible models while deeper requests can land on stronger options such as Mistral-Large-3 or gpt-5.4, with image, audio, and video inputs limited to models that explicitly support those modalities.
gist.visual_concept: Depict the tiered router as a cozy garden-path switchboard: three labeled paths, FAST, BALANCED, and DEEP, lead from a request terminal to different healthy model houses. Polli is the calm route keeper wearing tiny librarian glasses and consulting a glowing live-health map, while a CRT monitor robot eagerly points at green, healthy signal flowers; code-plants and modality icons for image, audio, and video show that the route is chosen from actual capability and health data rather than fixed destinations.
